name: com.nectarjobs/jobs
title: Nectar Jobs
description: Search 3M+ live job postings: salaries, filters, similar roles and CV matching. Free, no account.

tools.name: search_jobs
tools.description:
Search live job postings: use when the user asks what jobs are open for a role, a place,
    a salary or a skill. Each job carries ``url``, its page on Nectar Jobs, where the person applies.

    Args:
        query: keyword or natural-language query. Words that name an occupation ("manager",
            "software engineer") are matched against the TITLE; other words match the whole
            document (title, company, description), so a generic word's ``total`` overcounts —
            to compare role-type volumes, use aggregate_jobs instead.
        location: city or country substring over the posting's location text (matches broadly:
            "New York" includes the whole state). For a whole country, prefer ``country``.
        remote: filter to remote (true) or on-site (false) roles.
        salary_min: only roles whose salary range reaches this amount (raw number — currencies
            are not converted, so only meaningful combined with a single-currency market).
        company: company name substring.
        source: restrict to one source/board; get_stats lists the live sources and their sizes.
        seniority: one of intern, junior, senior, staff, principal, manager, director.
        category: job function from the site taxonomy (Engineering, "Data & ML", Product, Design,
            Sales, Marketing, "Customer Support", Operations, "Finance & Accounting",
            "People & HR", Legal, "IT & Security", …) — aggregate_jobs reports the live values.
        country: 2-letter ISO code ("US", "IN") — matches the derived country, more precise than
            a ``location`` substring.
        employment_type: contract or hours — permanent, fixed_term, contract, freelance, temporary,
            casual, seasonal, internship, apprenticeship, graduate, working_student, volunteer,
            self_employed, full_time, part_time, job_share, shift, term_time. Contract basis and
            schedule are one filter; a posting carries one of each. Note that a posting which says
            nothing about its hours is recorded as ``full_time``, so that value is the least
            informative of the set.
        posted_since_days: only jobs posted within this many days.
        mode: "hybrid" (default, best), "semantic" (meaning-based), or "keyword" (exact).
        sort: "relevance" (default), "date" (newest first), or "salary" (highest first).
        page: 1-based page number, for paging past ``limit`` results.
        limit: max results per page (1-100).
    Returns a dict with ``total``, a ``jobs`` list (duplicates collapsed) and ``attribution``;
    when nothing matched, a ``hint`` names the filter most worth loosening.

tools.name: aggregate_jobs
tools.description:
Aggregate counts for a filtered slice of the corpus — the tool for market/trend questions
    ("what kinds of roles are hiring in Pune?"), instead of issuing many limit-1 searches.

    Takes the same filters as search_jobs (keyword matching included, see its ``query`` note) and
    returns the slice's ``total`` plus breakdowns, each a {value: count} dict, biggest first:
    ``by_category`` (job function — the role-type axis), ``by_seniority``,
    ``by_employment_type`` (contract basis and hours in one axis; ``full_time`` is inflated because
    a posting silent about its hours is recorded as full-time), ``top_companies``,
    ``top_skills``, ``by_source``, ``benefits``, ``company_size``, ``lang``, and ``salary`` —
    per-currency posting counts with salary_max quartiles (currencies deliberately not blended).
    Every count collapses duplicate postings, so numbers are comparable to search totals. A
    breakdown on a field you filtered by lists only the values you filtered to.

tools.name: job_trends
tools.description:
How a slice of the market has changed OVER TIME — use this for "is X growing/shrinking",
    "hiring trend", "more or fewer than last year". aggregate_jobs describes a slice as it stands
    today; this one shows its history.

    Takes the same filters as aggregate_jobs, plus ``bucket`` ("day"/"week"/"month"),
    ``since_days`` (at most 730), and ``measure``. Returns a ``series``, oldest first, each period carrying
    ``postings`` (roles dated to it, duplicates collapsed) and ``still_open`` (how many are live
    now — the rest have since closed).

    ``measure="posted"`` (default) uses the employer's stated date: the market signal, but
    nullable, so check ``without_date`` — it counts roles the clock cannot place, and when it
    rivals the series totals the trend describes a minority of the slice.

    ``measure="first_seen"`` uses when we first crawled the row. Complete, but it measures OUR
    coverage: a backfill or a newly onboarded board appears as a spike of hundreds of thousands
    that is not a hiring event. Use it to audit ingestion, not to infer demand.

    Either way, periods before ``earliest`` are empty because we hold no data that far back, not
    because hiring stopped — never report that as a decline.

    CRITICAL for "posted": only compare periods at or after ``crawl_started``. Earlier ones are
    left-censored — the first crawl could only capture roles still live when it ran, so anything
    posted before that and already closed was never seen. Those buckets undercount severely (their
    ``still_open`` sits near 100%, the giveaway), and reading across the boundary turns the
    crawler's start date into a fake hiring boom.

tools.name: find_similar_jobs
tools.description:
Find jobs semantically similar to a given job (excludes its duplicates).

    At most ``max_per_company`` results per company (0 = uncapped; spellings of one employer, such
    as "Thales" and "Thales Group", count together), so one employer's near-identical
    postings don't fill the list; ``exclude_same_company`` drops the anchor's own company entirely
    ("roles like this elsewhere").

tools.name: recommend_jobs
tools.description:
Rank jobs by how well they match a résumé or free-text description of what
    the candidate wants. Returns the best-matching jobs first.

    ``country`` (ISO-2, e.g. GB) or ``location`` (a city or region) is REQUIRED — ask the seeker
    where they can work rather than guessing. Semantic ranking over every country returns the
    nearest postings on earth, most of which the person cannot take.

    ``resume_text``: only about the first 400 words shape the ranking; anything after them is not
    read. For a longer CV, send what defines the person's next role first: the role they want,
    their headline, their recent roles and their key skills, not the whole document in order.

    Ranking is purely semantic; the filters are hard. ``seniority`` (intern, junior, senior,
    staff, principal, manager, director) filters to exactly that tag — many postings carry none,
    so only pass it when the seeker insists.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description:
Fetch a single job's full details, including its description and any
    duplicate postings of the same role on other sources.

tools.name: get_stats
tools.description:
Return corpus-wide coverage: total jobs, counts by source, and top companies.
    For the same numbers on a filtered slice (a location, a company, a query), use
    aggregate_jobs.
